payload.title: The guard that keeps nestFactoryOptions from replacing the PII-masking kernel logger is a type-only excess-property check: a non-literal options value or a spread of Partial<NestApplicationOptions> compiles, and NestFactory.create still spreads nestFactoryOptions after the logger with no pin on that order
evidence: libs/backend-common/src/bootstrap/create-service-app.ts:128 (nestFactoryOptions is Omit<Partial<NestApplicationOptions>, 'logger'>, an all-optional type that rejects a logger key only on a fresh object literal)

libs/backend-common/src/bootstrap/create-service-app.ts:747-751 (NestFactory.create lists logger: new StructuredLoggerService first and spreads ...nestFactoryOptions after it, so a runtime logger key wins)
tests/invariants/structured-logger-single-authority.spec.ts:103-109 (the only text pin is toContain of the logger expression; it does not constrain its position against the spread)
tests/invariants/structured-logger-single-authority.spec.ts:112-129 (the type pin compiles fresh literals only; no variable, no spread, no Partial<NestApplicationOptions> value is tried)
apps/billing-service/src/main.ts:16 (a real caller passes a fresh literal with rawBody and bodyParser)
payload.rule_violated: OBS-CRITICAL-008 single redaction boundary (StructuredLoggerService is the only sink, per the header of structured-logger-single-authority.spec.ts) and the CLAUDE.md hierarchy: make the wrong behaviour impossible; a guard a non-literal bypasses is detection of literals only.
payload.notes: Reproduced on a local analog of the declaration at lines 128 and 747-751 (all-optional Omit type): { logger: false } and { rawBody: true, logger: ['error'] } are rejected, but `const widened = { rawBody: true, logger: false }` passed as the value, a `Partial<NestApplicationOptions>` variable, `{ ...wide }` and `{ ...widened }` are all accepted (a bare `{ logger: false }` variable fails only through the weak-type check, so adding one legitimate key lets it through). The three real callers (billing-service, event-store-service, gateway-api) pass fresh literals without logger, so nothing is wrong today, but any service that builds its options in a variable or spreads a Nest options object compiles, and line 750 then replaces the kernel logger: the service boots with logger false or a custom LoggerService and every Nest log line skips maskPii. The invariant stays green because it compiles literals only and the text pin ignores order. Close condition: Move `logger: new StructuredLoggerService(serviceName)` after `...rawBodyDefault, ...nestFactoryOptions` in the NestFactory.create call and extend structured-logger-single-authority.spec.ts with an AST position check that the logger property is the last property of that object literal; the pin then goes red if the spread is moved after it again. Plan row: DET detector program (landing batch 2b). Verified at head b2259fe03f of open pull request #2151; the cited code is not on main until that pull request merges.
